manuscript.title: An effective gbest-guided gravitational search algorithm for real-parameter optimization and its application in training of feedforward neural networks
manuscript.abstract_text: Gravitational search algorithm (GSA) is a recently introduced meta-heuristic that has shown great per- formance in numerical function optimization and solving real world problems. GSA provides an excellent social interaction between its search agents. This social interaction results in admirable exploration of the search space and gives a unique social component to GSA. However, the social interaction is not able to exploit good solutions in an eﬃcient manner. To overcome this problem, a novel algorithm named as gbest-guided gravitational search algorithm (GG-GSA) has been proposed by utilizing the global best (gbest) solution in the force calculation equation of GSA. The employment of gbest solution in any op- timization algorithm is a tough task and can lead to premature convergence. In the proposed algorithm, the gbest solution is used adaptively and is able to achieve a better trade-off between exploration and exploitation. The performance of the proposed algorithm is compared with GSA and its variants on dif- ferent suites of well-known benchmark test functions. The experimental results show that the GG-GSA performs better than other algorithms for most of the benchmark test functions. Furthermore, to test the ability of the proposed algorithm in solving real world applications, training of feedforward neural net- work problem is chosen. The results demonstrated the exceptional performance of GG-GSA on real world data-set.

In the last three decades nature inspired algorithms have been
widely investigated and applied to various real-world optimization
problems, e.g., image processing [1,2] , data clustering [3] , neural
network training [4,5] , graph theory [6] , economic dispatch [7] , etc.
Among the class of nature inspired algorithms, the gravitational
search algorithm (GSA) is a novel meta-heuristic search algorithm
proposed by Rashedi et al. [8] . This physics based algorithm is in-
spired by the Newtons’s law of gravity and motion. In GSA, the
search entities are group of masses (search agents) which com-
municate with each other on the basis of Newtonian gravity and
laws of the motion. In GSA, there are three main calculations, i.e.,
gravitational force calculation between different agents, accelera-
tion calculation and velocity calculation of each agent. In gravita-
tional force calculation, an agent tries to search for global optimum
by learning from K best selected agents. K best is a linearly decreas-

learning from K best agents results in the good exploration of the
search space but with the lapse of time only fewer agents are se-

In this way GSA is able to provide a good trade-off between explo-
ration and exploitation.
However, some researchers try to enhance the performance of
GSA by ﬁnding different ways for balancing exploration and ex-
ploitation. One common trend is to hybridize GSA with other ex-
isting metaheuristics. Mirjalili and Hashim [9] introduced a hybrid
approach by combining particle swarm optimization and gravita-
tional search algorithm (PSOGSA). In PSOGSA, the social thinking
of PSO is embedded into GSA. Li et al. [10] proposed a combination
of differential evolutionary algorithm and gravitational search algo-
rithm for unconstrained optimization problems. For image segmen-
tation, a novel hybrid genetic algorithm based gravitational search
algorithm was proposed by Sun and Zhang [11] . Jayaprakasam
et al. [12] proposed PSOGSA-E by adding the cognitive compo-
nent of PSO to PSOGSA algorithm and claimed that their proposed
algorithm can better deal with premature convergence problem.

exploration capability of GSA. In adaptive gbest-guided gravita-
tional search algorithm (GGSA), gbest-guidance inspired by PSO is
used to increase the velocity of the agents towards the memorized

the global best solution (gbest) is utilized adaptively to provide
a balance between exploration and exploitation. Modiﬁed gravi-
tational search algorithm (MGSA) [15] , employs the idea of local
best solution (pbest) and gbest solution taken from PSO into GSA
velocity calculation to enhance the exploration and exploitation of
GSA. Darzi et al. [16] raised the issue of losing optimal trajectory
in GSA as standard GSA does not store any solution into its mem-
ory. They introduced a new version of gravitational search algo-
rithm (MBGSA) based on memory which is inspired by PSO pbest
solutions. Recently, Sun et al. [17] modiﬁed the gravitational force
equation by adapting k local neighbors topology and also add the
guidance of global best agent (gbest) to propose locally informed
gravitational search algorithm (LIGSA). In LIGSA, every search agent
is getting guidance from its neighbor and gbest solution. Initially,
the priority is given to learning from neighbors for exploration
but, after certain number of iterations the search process is mainly
guided by gbest solution for enhanced exploitation. It has been
shown, that LIGSA is able to ﬁnd a better trade-off between ex-
ploration and exploitation than standard GSA and its variants.
Another common incline towards improvement of GSA perfor-
mance is to add some operators into the standard GSA. Disrup-
tion based operator was employed by Sarafrazi et al. [18] to further
adaptively explore and exploit the search space. Opposition-based
learning operator introduced by Shaw et al. [19] provides better
population initialization and also helps in improving the eﬃciency
of GSA to deal with local minima. Doraghinejad et al. [20] uti-
lized black hole theory to improve the exploration and exploitation
capabilities of GSA. However, there is an important concern that
above-mentioned variants of GSA seem to be diﬃcult to simulta-
neously achieve the balance between exploration and exploitation
of the GSA. Therefore, a good number of research attempts are re-
quired to establish new eﬃcient gravitational search algorithms for
optimization problems.
Motivated by the observations mentioned above, in this pa-
per a novel GSA variant, gbest-guided gravitational search algo-
rithm (GG-GSA) is proposed. In GG-GSA, a gbest-guidance is in-
troduced to emphasize the movement of search agents towards
the group-best solution (gbest solution) among the current pop-
ulation of agents, adaptively. For different real world problems, the
proposed algorithm can provide a better trade-off between explo-
ration and exploitation as compares to GSA and its variants. To
prove GG-GSA has better capabilities to search for optimal solution,
it is applied to well-known test functions. The proposed algorithm
has also been applied in training of feedforward neural networks
for classiﬁcation problems and its performance has been compared
with seven other state of the art algorithms. The results clearly
show that the proposed algorithm is able to ﬁnd better objective
function values in most of the considered classiﬁcation problems.
The goal of this paper is twofold.
• Firstly, a novel gbest-guided GSA is proposed and compared
with standard GSA and its recent variants on standard bench-
mark function problems.
• Secondly, a comparative study of the performance of GG-GSA
with respect to other state of the art metaheuristics on the
problem of training of feedforward neural networks (FNN).
The rest of the paper is organized as follows: Section 2 presents
the rudimentary concepts of FNN. Section 3 gives a brief review of
GSA while in Section 4 the proposed algorithm, GG-GSA is pre-
sented. In Section 5 , the performance of the proposed algorithm
is shown through experimental results. Section 6 depicts the ap-

3.1.

As mentioned previously, exploration and exploitation are the
two most common characteristics of population-based algorithms.
To attain the optimal solution, an algorithm must perform these
two vital process sensibly.
In GSA, initially, the value of the gravitational constant G is high
which results in fast movement of search agents. The good pace
of the agents explore the search space eﬃciently. To exploit the
good solutions in later iterations, the value of gravitational con-
stant G is decreases continuously as seen from Eq. (16) . The lower
value of G signiﬁcantly degrade the intensity of the attractive force
and unfortunately results in slow movement of search agents. The
slow movement of search agents negatively effects the convergence
speed and increases the chance of local stagnation [14] . The prob-
lem of slow movement of agents in later iterations can be seen
graphically in Fig. 2 .
Fig. 2 shows a hypothetical scenario of movement of search
agents in GSA. In these scenarios, the three agents having mass
M 1 , M 2 and M 3 are endeavoring to reach at global optimal solu-
tion. The three search agents are trying to attract each other with
a gravitational force that can be calculated by Eq. (14) . It can be
observed that at iteration t , mass M 1 is near to the optimal solu-
tion and possess more mass as compared to masses M 2 and M 3 .
At iteration t + 1 , the three masses move towards the center of
mass of other agents in the neighborhood instead of moving to-
wards the global optimal solution. The mass M 1 lost his ﬁtness to
some extent because of moving opposite to the optimal position
whereas, masses M 2 and M 3 are in the right direction. However,
due to deﬁciency of suﬃcient intensity of gravitational force, M 2
and M 3 cannot cross the position of M 1 to attain the optimal or
near optimal position. This phenomenon happens because of the
slow movement of masses (search agents) and results in poor con-
vergence. In iteration t + 2 , all the three masses converge in a po-
sition which is far from the global optimal solution.

sections.heading_text: Solution of slow movement of agents by GG-GSA
sections.body_text:
Basically, the proposed algorithm employs gbest-guidance to
enhance the exploitation of good solutions in the later iterations.
With the addition of gbest-component, the effective acceleration
of the search agents is also increased which helps GG-GSA to deal
with the problem of slow movement of agents.
In Fig. 4 , the position of agents at iteration t depict the same
scenario in which search agents of GSA converge in a sub-optimal
position due to the slow movement of agents. While dealing the
same situation, GG-GSA agents act differently than GSA. The pro-
posed algorithm calculates the gravitational force among search
agents using Eq. (21) . The addition of gbest-component and higher
values of acceleration coeﬃcients c 1 , c 2 increases the acceleration
of search agents in the later iteration as compared to GSA. That
high acceleration allows the GG-GSA agents to escape the local
stagnation. So, at iteration t + 1 , M 2 cross the position of M 1 as
the acceleration caused by intensity of the attracting gravitational
force is more. The agent having mass M 3 also comes near the op-
timal solution position whereas M 1 moves away from the optimal
position. At iteration t + 2 , M 1 cross the position of M 2 and has
reached near the global optimal position with M 2 and M 3 also
ends close to the optimal position. In this way, high acceleration
of search agents avoids the convergence at a sub-optimal position.

multi-modal functions with low dimensions. The detailed descrip-

The results of benchmark functions are averaged for 30 runs,

Category I: Unimodal functions . Functions f 1 to f 7 are unimodal
functions. From Table 2 , it can be observed that GG-GSA performs
better than GSA in 5 unimodal functions. In function f 6 both the
algorithms are able to reach global optima while in function f 7 ,
GG-GSA performance is competitive to GSA. The function f 7 is the
Quartic function (noisy), and it’s hard to ﬁnd the optimum solution
in presence of noise.
Category II: Multi-modal functions with high dimensions . Func-
tions f 8 to f 13 are multi-modal functions with high dimensions.
These functions provide a tough path for every optimization algo-
rithm because they contain large numbers of local optimum. It is
expected from every optimization algorithm to escape local optima
and converge near global optimum. The performance of GG-GSA is
better than GSA in all the multi-modal high dimension functions
except function f 12 . Moreover, the performance of the proposed al-
gorithm is exceptionally better than GSA in f 10 , f 11 and f 13 . In func-
tion f 8 and f 9 , the performance of GG-GSA is better than GSA, but
GSA is also showing competitive performance. In function f 12 , the
performance of GG-GSA is not good regarding average mean ﬁt-
ness, but it can be observed that the best ﬁtness achieved by GG-
GSA is far better than GSA, which shows the level of optimization
GG-GSA can achieve.
Category III: Multi-modal functions with low dimensions . Func-
tions f 14 to f 23 are the multi-modal functions with low dimensions.
These functions possess a less number of local optimum as com-
pared to category II functions but, the robustness of optimization
algorithms can be analyzed on these functions. Out of the ten func-
tions in this category, in 6 functions the performance of GG-GSA
and GSA is at par. In function f 14 , f 15 , f 21 and f 23 , one can see the
better results shown by the proposed algorithm which proves that
GG-GSA is better than GSA concerning robustness also. In these
four functions, GSA is not able to maintain its robustness and mis-
erably in few runs it deviates from global optima.

sections.body_text:
In this section, the performance of GG-GSA is investigated on all
benchmark functions of the CEC 2014 competition on Single Objec-
tive Real Parameter Optimization [39] . The benchmark suite con-
tains 4 types of function i.e., unimodal, multi-modal, hybrid and
composition function. The summary of the benchmark functions of
CEC 2014 is given in Table A.16 (see appendix) and the parameter
settings is given in Table 5 .
On the test functions, the proposed algorithm is compared with
GSA and its recent variants which have used gbest guidance or
includes modiﬁcation in the force calculation of GSA. In the ex-
periments, both 30 and 50-dimensional problems were consid-
ered and the maximum number of function evaluations was set to
30,0 0 0 for every algorithm to ensure the fair comparison. Table 6
present the simulation results on CEC 2014 benchmark functions.
Here, the value in bold for “Mean” indicate the algorithm ex-
hibiting the best performance among the considered methods for
comparison.
To ﬁnd the signiﬁcant difference in performance of multiple al-
gorithms, Derrac et al. [41] provides several methods. In this study,
Friedman test is selected to ﬁnd the signiﬁcant difference in per-
formance of considered competitive algorithms followed by post-
hoc tests.

Category B: Multi-modal functions . The benchmark functions

also shifted and rotated which makes the ﬁnding of global op-

multi-modal problems can be summarized as follows:
• In functions f 105 , f 107 , f 112 –114 almost all the algorithms perform
equally in both 30 and 50 dimension problems, while in func-

difference in performances of algorithms.
• In 30 dimension problems, GG-GSA produced best mean accu-

f 106 , f 110 –111 , f 113 and f 115 –116 .
• In 50 dimension problems, GG-GSA produced best mean accu-

f 106 , f 107 , f 110 –111 , and f 114 –116 .
• It is evident from the results of multi-modal functions that in
higher dimension problems, the performance of GG-GSA is su-
perior than other competitive algorithms.
Category C: Hybrid functions . It should be noted that in hybrid
functions the variables are randomly divided into some subcom-
ponents and then different basic functions are used for different
subcomponents [39] , results in the signiﬁcant downfall of the per-
formance of optimization algorithms. The same is evident by re-
sults of GSA, MGSA, GGSA, and LIGSA. The performance of GG-GSA
still remains competitive as it was in basic functions. It can be eas-
ily observed that the quality of the results produced by GG-GSA
is very high in hybrid functions f 117 , f 120 , and f 121 . In 30 dimen-
sion problems, out of 6 hybrid functions, GG-GSA outperformed
other algorithms in 4 functions whereas, in 50-dimensional prob-

hybrid functions. These results evident that as compare to other al-
gorithms GG-GSA is able to handle well the increase in dimension
of problems. Moreover, the performance of the proposed algorithm
is exceptionally well in the hybrid group of functions.

to the mark as it was in previous functions because of the com-
plexity of these functions. But, again the high standard of quality
of solutions of GG-GSA can be observed in functions f 129 and f 130
in 30 dimension problems as compared to other comparative al-
gorithms. Here, GG-GSA ﬁnds best results in 4 out of 8 functions
in both 30 and 50 dimension problems. To be speciﬁc, the per-
formance of GG-GSA in composition benchmark function is best
among the ﬁve algorithms. The performance of the proposed algo-

7.4462E −11 and 3.8293E −17 respectively, that clearly shows the

algorithms. According to Friedman test results, a post-hoc statisti-

Hochberg, Hommel, Holland, Rom, Finner, and Li are employed to
detect signiﬁcant difference between GG-GSA (control algorithm)
and rest of the algorithms. The details and source code for apply-
ing these procedures is available in [42] . Tables 8 and 9 show all
the p -Values for each comparison which involves the control algo-
rithm. After conducting the multiple comparison analysis by using
the mean objective value of CEC 2014 functions, it can be observe
that:
• According to Holm, Hommel, Holland, and Finner post-hoc
tests, GG-GSA is signiﬁcantly better than GSA, GGSA, MGSA and
LIGSA on both 30 and 50 dimensional problems.
• According to Hochberg, Rom, and Li post-hoc tests, GG-GSA per-
forms signiﬁcantly better than GSA, GGSA, and MGSA, but it
behaves equally to LIGSA on both 30 and 50 dimensional prob-
lems.
• Overall on the basis of multiple comparison analysis, the per-
formance of the proposed algorithm is superior as compare to
rest of the competitors.
Among the other competitors, GG-GSA exhibits the best per-
formance on the whole CEC 2014 benchmark function suite both
in 30 and 50-dimensional problems. However, the performance of
the proposed algorithm is not good enough in solving the com-
plex problems like composition functions. In this study, our aim is
to test the performance of GG-GSA with a simple framework on
distinct benchmark functions. By adding more sophisticated mech-
anism or by introducing some powerful operators of other heuris-
tics, GG-GSA can also exhibit better performance in complex prob-
lems.
5.2.2.

In this section, the computational eﬃciency of the above ﬁve
algorithms has been compared. On the basis of mean computa-
tional time consumed by each algorithm for one independent run
in solving the benchmark functions of CEC 2014, the algorithms
are ranked as GSA < GGSA < MGSA < GG-GSA < LIGSA. The
standard GSA spends the least time on all benchmark functions
followed by GGSA, MGSA, GG-GSA and LIGSA. GG-GSA takes a lit-
tle more time than GSA, GGSA and MGSA because in GG-GSA,
gbest solution is utilized in force calculation equation which posses
O( n 3 ) complexity whereas in GGSA and MGSA, gbest solution is
employed in velocity calculation which takes O( n 2 ) complexity.
The computational time of LIGSA is worst among its competitors,
the reason behind this phenomenon is that different number of
complex calculations are included in it. Except LIGSA, rest of the
four competitors only checks for position constraint on solutions
whereas, LIGSA checks the velocity constraints and solution dupli-
cation constraint also. Among different constraints, to check the
availability of duplicate solutions is the most complex with com-
putational complexity O( n 3 ) consequently increasing the computa-
tional time. With analysis of computational time of all competi-
tive algorithms, it is observed that the proposed algorithm takes
slightly more computational time than GSA, GGSA and MGSA but
also counter it with good optimization performance as evident by
results in Tables 6 and 7 .
6.

sections.heading_text: Application of GG-GSA in training of feedforward neural network (multi-layer perceptron)
sections.body_text:
In this section, the proposed GG-GSA algorithm is applied to
solve the problem of training FNN. First, the design of FNN is dis-
cussed along with the representation of search agents and then,
the experimental setup is presented along with results and discus-
sion.
6.1.

sections.heading_text: Design of FNN and vector formation of GG-GSA search agents
sections.body_text:
While designing the FNN, the main issue is to decide the num-
ber of hidden layers and the number of nodes in each layer. As
there is no standard method to select these two parameters, the
method proposed by [4,43] is followed in which single hidden
layer FNN is considered with number of neurons calculated by the
formula: 2 × n + 1, where n is the number of input features in
the dataset.
In application of GG-GSA for training of FNN, each search agent
of the proposed approach consist of three parts: ﬁrst part con-
tains the set of biases, second part consists the weights linking
the input layer nodes to hidden layer and the last part comprise
of the weights linking hidden layer nodes to output layer. The for-
mation of search agent as a vector is diagrammatically represented
in Fig. 6 . In Fig. 6 , there are n number of input nodes, 2 × n + 1 =
m number of hidden layer nodes and only one output node. More
details about the FNN architecture for the considered datasets can
be found in [44] .
6.2.

Tables 11 and 12 report the average classiﬁcation accuracy
of the eight algorithms on different datasets. The datasets of
Table 11 are having low number of input features. As shown in
Table 11 , the proposed algorithm is able to achieve the best classi-
ﬁcation accuracy in four datasets i.e., Cancer, Diabetes, Diagnosis I
and Diagnosis II. In the two datasets Blood and Vertebral, GG-GSA
stood rank two in terms of average classiﬁcation accuracy whereas
WOA ranked one in them. From these results it can be concluded
that the proposed algorithm is showing a very good competitive
performance in datasets having less number of input features.
Table 12 reports the performance of all the competitors in
datasets having higher number of input features (9 or more).
These high dimensional datasets can check the exploration per-
formance of the algorithms. From results of Table 12 , it is very
clear that the proposed algorithm GG-GSA is able to outperform
all the other competitors. In 7 out of 8 datasets, the proposed al-
gorithm achieves the best accuracy rate. The GG-GSA based FNN
trainer not only outperforms other trainer but also achieves a sig-
niﬁcant increase in the classiﬁcation accuracy rate which is evident
by the results of datasets like Tic-tac-toe, Ring, Ionosphere, Chess
and Biodegradation. From these results, it is evident that in high
dimension classiﬁcation problems GG-GSA is the best FNN trainer
among all the competitive FNN training algorithms.
The reason for the good performance of the proposed algorithm
in high dimensional datasets is its enhanced exploration and ex-
ploitation capability which works as follows:
• In the initial iterations, the proposed algorithm works in a sim-
ilar manner just like standard GSA because initially the value of
acceleration coeﬃcient c 2 is almost equal to zero which makes
gbest component inactive. However, the use of acceleration co-
eﬃcient c 1 with initial value equals to two doubles the acceler-
ation of the search agents which result in better exploration of
the search space. In high dimensional data the exploration ca-
pability of the algorithms is tested and the proposed algorithm
has shown distinctively good performance.
• With lapse of iterations, the value of c 2 increases and gbest
component start attracting the search agents towards best so-
lutions. This results in better exploitation of good solutions and
the proposed algorithm converge on or near to optimal solu-
tion.

7.

Gravitational based search algorithms are useful to solve many
real life problems therefore, a novel gbest-guided gravitational
search algorithm (GG-GSA) is proposed in this work. Here, a com-
pletely new deﬁnition of gravitational force calculation is devel-
oped by providing gbest-guidance to the existing formulation. The
performance of the proposed algorithm is compared with GSA on
23 popular benchmark functions. The results show that GG-GSA
outperformed GSA in ﬁnding optimal solutions with better con-
vergence speed. Complexity analysis of the proposed algorithm
has also performed and it has been found that GG-GSA is having
the same complexity like GSA. Furthermore, GG-GSA is also com-
pared with GSA and its recent variants GGSA, MGSA, and LIGSA on
modern CEC 2014 benchmark function suite, the results of which
show that the performance of GG-GSA on whole CEC 2014 bench-
mark function suite is best. Finally, it is demonstrated that GG-GSA
can be used to solve the problem of training of feedforward neu-
ral networks. Experiments were performed on 16 standard clas-
siﬁcation problems and it is evident by the results that the pro-
posed algorithm is very eﬃcient in training of FNN which is due
to the presence of good trade-off between exploration and ex-
ploitation. It has been also observed that results of FNN trained
by GG-GSA were much better in datasets having high dimensions.
The performance of the proposed algorithm in training of FNN es-
tablish its suitability and effectiveness in dealing with real world
problems.
In future GG-GSA can be applied on constrained optimization
and multi-objective problems. To see the effectiveness of the pro-
posed algorithm in training of other type of neural networks and
multi-class classiﬁcation problems is a good area to explore. By
adding some mathematical operator of other heuristics into the
GG-GSA like crossover, mutation, chaotic perturbation, etc., is also
an area of study to further enhance the performance of GG-GSA.

gbest-guided gravitational search algorithm (GGSA), gbest-guidance inspired by PSO is used to increase the velocity of the agents towards the memorized best solution for gaining better convergence speed [14]
